method: Document the complete integration and live acceptance contract from current production implementations and recent launch failures; do not change runtime or strategy.
owner_request: New competitors have repeatedly required manual recovery because integration, watchdog, data freshness, scheduler, scoreboard, Discord, updater, and live-verification requirements are scattered.
before_state: Four traders are live, but no single end-to-end add-a-trader runbook exists; recent SURGE/GROK launch incidents exposed port collision, stopped retry wrapper, after-hours startup rejection, SQLite scheduler threading, and stale shared bars.
reason: New competitors have repeatedly required manual recovery because integration, watchdog, data freshness, scheduler, scoreboard, Discord, updater, and live-verification requirements are scattered.
intended_scope: Add one repository documentation file only, plus mandatory governance lifecycle records. Describe ownership boundary, wiring map, templates/contracts, deployment and launch, restart safety, health telemetry, failure diagnosis, and a hard live acceptance checklist.
expected_effects: Future agents can add a trader without copying private strategy or declaring success before process, cycles, evidence, official ledger, and Discord surfaces are all verified.
required_tests: Validate every cited path and command exists; inspect rendered Markdown; run documentation contract/static checks if present; git diff review.
risks: Documentation can become stale; mitigate with explicit source-of-truth paths, invariants, and a maintenance checklist rather than embedding volatile implementation details without anchors.
next_safe_action_if_interrupted: Inspect all current trader launch, watchdog, roster, scoreboard, Discord, data, deployment, and test integration points; author and validate the runbook.
